messages:
anne: Quick proposal — introduce an "elastic lanes" feature for Dedicated reserved pools. Lightweight burst affordance that gives short, predictable overage capacity with preemption and clear billing rules. Wanted to get quick reactions on launch criteria + autoscale interactions. :thinking:

anne: High-level idea: each reserved pool can opt-in to 1–2 elastic lanes (fast/slow). Lanes allow short bursts beyond the committed capacity (e.g., up to 3x) for a short window (30–120s). Bursts consume "burst tokens" that are either prepaid (carryover credits) or billed as overage. When capacity is tight, lane allocations are preemptable and degrade gracefully to a fallback model variant or lower-QoS queue.

anne: Questions for the group: what safety signals do we need to launch (SLOs, max eviction rate, cost delta)? What should autoscale do while a lane is active? How do we surface this in the Console / SLA docs?

dave: I like the carrier-lane idea. Implementation note: easiest path is to treat lanes as soft reservations with a low-priority instance pool. Autoscaler can either a) spin up ephemeral nodes when bursts exceed commit, or b) steal existing headroom. Option a is cleaner for isolation but costs more ops. :+1:

dave: Proposal: pilot uses option (a) with ephemeral nodes + cooldown (5m) to avoid churn. We can later add opportunistic reuse if customers care about cost.

maria: Safety signals: 99th- and 99.9th-percentile latency for burst requests, % of bursts that get preempted, and customer visible error rate. We should block on >0.5% user-facing evictions during bursts for pilot customers. Also need to ensure no cross-tenant noisy-neighbor amplification. :eyes:

kevin: From a contract standpoint we need clear language: "elastic lanes are best-effort, preemptable, and billed separately as burst credits or overage." Also decide if bursts are included in Dedicated commit calculations (my vote: separate). Customers will want predictable pricing and a way to opt-out.

sophie: Console + UX: show a per-pool "burst budget" meter, historical burst usage graph, and post-burst breakdown (tokens used, cost, preemptions). Add a toggle for lane enable + lane policy (max multiplier, window length, preemption priority). Also surface a tooltip: "Lanes are best-effort and may be preempted to preserve committed capacity."

dave: Config sketch (pilot):
```
{"pool_id": "pool-1234",
 "elastic_lanes": [{
   "name": "fast",
   "max_multiplier": 3,
   "window_secs": 60,
   "token_mode": "prepaid", // or "on_demand"
   "preemption_priority": 100
 }]
}
```

maria: Preemption policy: recommend token-based aging + fairness. Each burst alloc consumes a token with TTL; when system is pressured, eviction sorts by (preemption_priority, token_age, tenant_priority_score). That keeps deterministic behavior and lets us give customers a concrete eviction exposure number in the SLA.

anne: Autoscale interaction: during bursts the autoscaler should NOT immediately scale the committed pool unless configured. Pilot default: spin up ephemeral nodes from a separate ephemeral fleet that are labeled "burst-only". If bursts persist beyond X windows (configurable, e.g., 10m), then flag for ops and suggest a capacity bump or change to commit.

kevin: Billing modes: 1) prepaid credits (monthly carryover), 2) pay-as-you-go burst overage, 3) included small allowance. Need to map to sales SKUs.

sophie: UX question: how do we let tenants test without affecting billing? Maybe sandbox mode: bursts allowed but billed to test credits and visible in Console as "test usage".

dave: Dev checklist for pilot: feature flag, ephemeral fleet + scaling hooks, preemption comparator, telemetry events (burst.start, burst.end, preempt.evicted, cost.charge). Add a canary with 3 pools (one small, one mid, one enterprise-sized).

anne: Launch criteria proposal (pilot->beta):
- pilot run for 4 weeks with 3 customers
- <0.5% user-facing evictions during bursts
- measurable cost delta per pool <10% for typical burst traffic patterns
- telemetry in Console + billing export enabled
- contract language + opt-out UI live

maria: Also require postmortem-runbook and automatic alert when preemption rate >0.2%/hour for any pool in pilot.

kevin: Sales needs a short one-pager describing tradeoffs and pricing bands. I can draft once we lock billing modes.

anne: Timeline suggestion: 2 sprint implementation (runtime + autoscale hooks), 1 sprint for Console + billing + docs, then pilot. Owner: dave (eng) for runtime, sophie (DX) for console, kevin (sales) for contract, maria (sre) for safety gating.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-flag scaffolding to canary org tomorrow 18:00 UTC. :rocket:

anne: Awesome — thanks all. Action items: dave to post PR link and rough ETA, sophie to prototype UI mockups, kevin will prepare draft contract text, maria will write alerting playbook. We'll reconvene in 1 week. :+1:

kevin: sounds good.

maria: added alerting playbook draft to docs repo, will share link in the thread when ready.

anne: Meeting scheduled (optional): Fri 09:30 to align pilot customers. Invite sent.

sophie: mockups incoming by EOD Thursday.
